conflict_topics: coverage for the working day before Chinese New Year (first day)
coverage for the working day after Chinese New Year (second day)
method for deciding who stays (draw lots vs other solutions)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concise personal reasons (childcare, family trip, reunion dinner) which ground their requests (e.g. Turn 2, Turn 9, Turn 4).
C negotiates conditionally (offers work in exchange for Christmas leave), which clarifies tradeoffs (Turn 11 / 23).
Group moves from arguing about decision method (draw lots) to a practical external solution (ask head office), which is a reasonable problem-solving shift (Turn 18 onward).
evaluation.final_reason: The team reached a concrete, mutual spoken agreement in Round 11: Agent C said, "So if we get a temp for that day, the deal is on. I'll work the New Year days, and I get Christmas." Agent A accepted this and they agreed to wait for head office. Agent B had also volunteered to contact head office earlier (Turn 22: "Okay, I'll email head office now and ask."). Thus the staff resolved their internal allocation by compromising (C trades working the New Year days for Christmas) contingent on third-party intervention (head office supplying a temp).
position_change_notes: Agent C moved from offering conditional help to an explicit conditional commitment: initially "I can work the New Year days if I can have Christmas off" (Turn 3 / 11) and later reiterated as a deal (Turn 23).
Agent B initially insisted on needing the first day for childcare (Turn 2), later accepted the plan to ask head office and to pursue the external solution (Turn 22).
Agent A consistently stated they could not work (Turn 1, Turn 9) and did not change that; A accepted the group's conditional arrangement (Turn 25).
Agent D consistently could not work the first day (Turn 4, Turn 8, Turn 16) and rejected random allocation; D agreed to pursue asking head office (Turn 20).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1-2: Agent A: "I need those two days off around New Year." Agent B: "I need the first day off. My son's childcare is closed." (Overlapping leave needs create a staffing problem.)

Turn 3-4: Agent C offers a conditional trade (will work if gets Christmas off) and Agent D: "The first day is reunion dinner for my family." (Now three people have conflicts with the first day; coverage looks impossible unless someone changes.)
Turn 5-6: Agent A: "So all three of us need that first day." Agent B: "I can work the second day. It's just the first one I need." (Confirms three unavailable for the first day; no resolution.)
Turn 7-8: Agent C: "We still need one more person for the first day with me." Agent D: "I cannot work on the first day." (Still lacking sufficient staff for the first day.)
Turn 9-10: Agent A: "My family's trip starts that day. I also can't work." Agent B: "So all three of us can't work on the first day. How do we solve this?" (Problem restated and unresolved.)

Turn 11,13: Agent C: "I can work that day, but only if my Christmas leave is approved." Agent A: "How do we decide then? Draw lots?" (Conditional offer and a contested decision method; no settlement.)

Turn 14,16: Agent B: "I'm not comfortable with that. If I don't get the day off, I have a real problem with childcare." Agent D: "I don't want to draw lots either. I can't risk missing my family dinner." (Participants reject the random allocation idea; conflict over method remains.)

Turn 17-18: Agent A: "So if we're not drawing lots, what's the alternative?" Agent B: "We could ask head office if they can get a temp in for the day. That way we could all take it." (A concrete solution is proposed, reducing direct internal conflict though it depends on an external actor.)

Turn 19-20: Agent C: "That's a good idea. If head office can send someone, that solves the problem." Agent D: "Yes, let's ask." (Agreement on the proposed plan; remaining issue is pending head-office approval.)
Turn 21-22: Agent A: "Okay, let's ask. It's worth a try." Agent B: "Okay, I'll email head office now and ask." (Team commits to asking head office; outcome still pending.)

Turn 23-25: Agent C: "So if we get a temp for that day, the deal is on. I'll work the New Year days, and I get Christmas." Agent A: "Right. So we wait to hear back." (A clear, mutual, concrete agreement among staff: C will work the New Year days in exchange for Christmas leave, contingent on head office supplying a temp; the group accepts this arrangement.)
Round 12: No public speech or observable action. (No new conflict; the previously reached conditional agreement stands in the transcript.)

substantive_insights: The core incompatibility was practical staffing: three staff needed the same day off, leaving only one potential person available unless someone changed plans.
C's leverage was a conditional offer (work the New Year days in exchange for Christmas leave), creating a clear internal trade that allowed the group to agree.
The team relied on a third party (head office/temp) to remove the structural impossibility; internal agreement was conditional on that external approval.
